title: Warehouse SKU codes
prompt: The warehouse labels active products with a SKU such as `HOM-P0077`: a category prefix, the product id and a check digit. Write `solve(products)` so it returns `product_id`, `name` and `sku` for every active product.
rules: Only products whose `active` is true; inactive products and those with a missing `active` are left out.
The SKU is the first three letters of `category` in capitals (all of it if it's shorter), a hyphen, the `product_id`, then the check digit.
The check digit is the sum of the digits in `product_id`, modulo 10: `P007` gives 7 and `P099` gives 8 (9 + 9 = 18).
If `category` or `product_id` is missing, `sku` is missing. Return `product_id`, `name` and `sku`, all text, in that order.
hints: Keep the active products with `filter` first. Built-ins handle the prefix: `F.upper(F.substring("category", 1, 3))`.
The check digit is plain Python: `sum(int(c) for c in product_id if c.isdigit()) % 10`. Wrap it in a UDF that returns text and handles `None`.
`F.concat` joins the pieces, `F.lit("-")` included, and gives NULL when any piece is NULL.
explanation: Filter on `F.col("active") == True` (a missing flag isn't true, so it drops out), then build the SKU with `F.concat(F.upper(F.substring("category", 1, 3)), F.lit("-"), F.col("product_id"), check_digit("product_id"))`, where `check_digit` is a string UDF returning `None` for a missing id and the digit sum modulo 10 otherwise. Only the check digit needs Python; the rest are built-ins, which also make a missing category give a missing SKU. Forgetting `% 10` gives two digits for ids like `P099`.
starter:
